CORRECTION, LEFT VISIBLE. This archive carried this household as «Francesco COSSI & Maria Falco» from 1823 to 1828. It is CIOFFI. The 1825 register, read at full resolution, writes the strada Camellara family with a dotted «i» after the C — «Cesare Cioffi», «Francesco Cioffi», «Giuseppa Cioffi» — and writes the strada Cossi family, in the same volume and the same hand, without one: «Domenico Cossi», «Crescenzo Cossi», «strada Cossi». Two different families, distinguished by the clerk and conflated by this archive. Everything else about the household stands.

A contadino, dead before July 1843. Named only in his son's death act. Note the forename: a GIOACCHINO FALCO, thirty-six, declares on strada Camellara in 1816 and is a candidate fifth child of Matteo Falco — the name runs in both houses, which is suggestive and nothing more.

Forty-seven, a contadino of strada Camellara. THIRTEEN MONTHS LATER, at forty-eight, the same man reports the death of CHIARA RIVETTI on the same street. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco four different ages, this one holds. He is a neighbour; the act does not call him kin, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.

A contadino of STRADA CAMELLARA — the street of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti. He is one of the two men who report CHIARA RIVETTI'S DEATH on 3 September 1843. He declares on that street across four volumes, and his stated age is, after the first entry, the steadiest series in these registers: FORTY in 1840, FORTY-SEVEN in August 1842, FORTY-EIGHT in September 1843. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco eleven different ages, this clerk got one right. HE IS A NEIGHBOUR. No act calls him kin to the Falco, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.
«È morto nella sua propria casa LUIGI CIOFFI DI UN GIORNO.» One day old.
«È morta nella sua propria casa MADDALENA CIOFFI D'UN ANNO.» One year old. The earliest of the three acts.
«È morta nella sua propria casa MARTA CIOFFI D'UN MESE.» One month old. Declared by Clemente Cioffi and Virgilio Cioffi, both of strada Camellara — a fourth and fifth Cioffi on the Falco street.
A contadino of strada Cioffi, named without «fu» in all three acts. He appears in person as a declarant in Morti 1842 atto 80, aged THIRTY-SIX, which would put his birth about 1806.

«figlia di FRANCESCO COSSI, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi» — named without «fu», so living

«GIUSEPPA COSSI, di mesi otto, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, figlia di FRANCESCO COSSI, di professione Contadino, e di MARIA FALCO» — the third child of this house to die in three years, all three declared by GIUSEPPE FALCO of strada Camellara.

«GIUSEPPE CRISCI(?), di anni cinque, nato in Arienzo, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, figlio di FRANCESCO COSSI, di professione contadino, e di MARIA FALCO» — a second child of this house to die, after Antonia in June 1823. THE SURNAME IS AMBIGUOUS IN THE HAND: it can be read Cossi or Crisci, and the 1823 act was read Cossi. Recorded as Cossi with the doubt stated. Note that the household is here on STRADA CAMELLARA, where the 1823 act placed it on strada Sant'Andrea.
Seven months old — the fifth child of this household to be buried since 1823. The act is the one in which GIUSEPPE FALCO is entered as «PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA».

«ANGELA FALCO di anni cinquantuno, vedova di CRESCENZO RIVETTI … figlia di MATTEO FALCO Defunto … e di FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta» — she outlived Crescenzo by nearly six years and had moved from strada Camellara to strada Capodiuomo. Declared by Nicola Maggione and Alessandro Martone, both twenty-two and both «vicino della defunta». HER PARENTAGE EXPLAINS THE 1816 ACT: when Crescenzo died, GIOACCHINO FALCO and GIUSEPPE FALCO declared it as «parenti del defunto» — they were his wife's brothers.

line.name: Carmine Antonio (Carminantonio) Falco
line.note: Born at Arienzo, resident in the province of Benevento, died at Brisbane and buried at Nudgee Cemetery in niche CHAP-082-B2. His wife Filomena Annecchino died on 10 August 1988 and lies beside him in B1. Two of their sons, Carmine and Raffaele, married two Zampiello sisters of Arpaia and both brought their families to Brisbane.

line.name: Carmine Antonio Falco

line.name: Carmine Falco
line.note: Born at Forchia in the Valle Caudina. He and Francesca reached Brisbane on the ss «Sydney» of the Lauro Lines, out of Naples, arriving 26 MARCH 1964 — the Quarantine Service passenger list of that voyage enters them at numbers 492 and 493, bound for 43 Mount Joy, Petrie Terrace, Brisbane, an address given on 2 September 1963. Two further passengers of the same surname travel with them and are withheld here. The archive previously said «about 1957»; that was an inference from the 1957–1977 span of their Brisbane immigration file, and the passenger list corrects it. Francesca died at Brisbane on 10 September 2022 and is buried at Nudgee, plot V-0949.

events.evidence: «è morto nella sua propria casa CLEMENTE FALCO, di mesi QUINDICI, nato in Arienzo, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO, di professione contadino, e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA» — born about March 1824, a child of this house the archive did not have. HE DIED NINETEEN DAYS AFTER HIS SISTER MADDALENA, who was seven. Declared by MARCELLO COSSI, 35, and ANIELLO DIGLIO, 50, both of strada Camellara — Diglio is the same neighbour who stood with Giuseppe in April, when he was given as forty-six.

«Domenico Falco figlio di Giuseppe Falco, e Gelsomina Vigliotta» — died at twelve o'clock, aged about two years and four months; he was born 25 November 1816. Declared by Francesco Martone, cantiniere, and Michele Bordica, 27, contadino, both «nella Camellara, vicini».

«figlio di GIOACCHINO CIOFFI defunto, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, E DI FRANCESCA FALCO defunta» — from the death act of her son Aniello Cioffi, 27 July 1843, verified at full resolution. Her son was seventy-six, so born about 1767, which places her marriage in the seventeen-sixties and her own birth in the seventeen-forties: the generation of MATTEO FALCO himself. NOTHING NAMES HER PARENTS and this archive does not guess at them.

Named in THREE acts, all without «fu», so alive throughout: Morti 1840 atto 50 (17 Aug 1840), Morti 1842 atto 2 (2 Jan 1842) and Morti 1843 atto 17 (10 Jun 1843). The 1843 act was read at strip resolution and published as «DOMENICA Falco» — explicitly flagged at the time as a hypothesis, not a finding. The 1840 and 1842 acts, both read at 2600–2800px, give FRANCESCA. The correction stands beside the error in the notes rather than replacing it. NO ACT NAMES HER PARENTS, and the archive does not guess at them. She is NOT the older Francesca Falco who married Gioacchino Cioffi and whose son died at seventy-six in 1843 — that woman was born in the 1740s; this one is bearing children in 1840. Two women, two generations apart, each married to a Cioffi.

Josephum Falco filium Matthei, e Franciscae Crisci — son of Matteo — and in June 1818 he declares a daughter's birth as a contadino of STRADA CAMELLARA, aged 36, which puts his own birth about 1782 and places a documented son of Matteo Falco on the family's street.

«e di Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentadue, massaro di campagna, domiciliato ugualmente nel luogo indicato» — declaring the death of Crescenzo Rivetti alongside Gioacchino Falco, the two of them «parenti del defunto». PLACED HERE WITH RESERVATION: the street matches this household, but the age does not. This man is 32 in December 1816; the Giuseppe of strada Camellara is 36 in June 1818, which would make him 34 here. The trade differs too — massaro di campagna against contadino. It may be the same man loosely aged, or a third Giuseppe.

«Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasette, di professione massaro di campagna, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — twice in five days: on 24 October for a neighbour, Marianna Petrillo, and on 28 October for Vincenzo Falco's infant son Raffaele, where he and Sabato Vassallo are called «PARENTI». Vincenzo is a grandson of Matteo; Giuseppe is a documented son of Matteo, which would make him Vincenzo's uncle — and the register's own word for the relationship is kin. Aged 37 here, so born about 1780.

«e di Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasei, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — declaring the death of a neighbour, Emanuela d'Onofrio, with Domenico Balletta, 40, sartore, of the same street. THIS IS THE SIGHTING THAT TIES THE OTHERS TOGETHER: one month later, on 7 June 1818, the birth act of his daughter Maddalena gives him as thirty-six, contadino, of strada Camellara, husband of Antonia di Guida. Same age, same trade, same street, four weeks apart — one man, not two. Balletta is his neighbour in October 1817 as well.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantatre, di professione Contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato strada Camellara» — THE FIRST CIVIL RECORD TO STATE HIS PARENTAGE OUTRIGHT. The clerk adds «fu Matteo» to tell him from the other Giuseppe Falco of the town, and in doing so confirms from the civil series what the archive previously had only from the parish books: this Giuseppe is a son of the late Matteo Falco. Forty-three here, so born about 1780 — which agrees with the thirty-seven he gives in October 1817. He declares with Cesare Giglio, 50, of the same street, at the death of Maria Crisci, three years old, daughter of Marcello Crisci and Maria Rosa Mauro.

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantadue, di professione Contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Sant'Andrea, vicino della defunta» — atto 39, the SECOND «fu Matteo» sighting in two days, at the death of Antonia Cossi, nine months old, daughter of Francesco Cossi and a MARIA FALCO. TWO CAUTIONS. He is forty-two here and forty-three the day before, from the same clerk — a plain measure of how loosely these ages are kept. And he is given here on STRADA SANT'ANDREA where the day before he is on strada Camellara: in this form a declarant described as «vicino» is recorded at the street of the house where the death happened, so a declarant's street is NOT reliable evidence of where he himself lived.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, vicino del defunto» — declaring beside his brother PASQUALE FALCO. The only act found so far in which the two brothers appear together, and the first to give Giuseppe's trade as colono rather than contadino. Forty-two here, so born about 1782.

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO, regnicolo, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino della defunta, ed ANIELLO DIGLIO, di anni quarantasei, contadino» — a seventh sighting, and THE THIRD TIME HE STANDS FOR THE SAME HOUSE. Francesco Cossi and Maria Falco lost Antonia in June 1823, Giuseppe in March 1824 and Giuseppa here in April 1825, and Giuseppe Falco declared every one. The register calls him «vicino» each time and never «parente», so nothing states a relationship — but three appearances for one household is a pattern, and it is the best hint yet that this Maria Falco is his kin. His trade drifts again: contadino in 1823, colono in 1824, MASSARO here; and his age goes backwards, forty here against forty-two the year before.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTASEI, di professione MASSARO, regnicolo, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino del Defunto» — declaring atto 56, the death of Giuseppe Cossi, two, son of Gaspare Cossi and Maria Sposito. Aged 46, so born about 1780; he was 37 and «massaro di campagna» on the same street in October 1817.

Declaring atto 73 TOGETHER WITH CARLANTONIO MORGILLO, 46, contadino, of the same street — the FIRST ACT IN THE WHOLE ARIENZO SERIES in which a Falco and a Morgillo stand side by side. Both are entered as «vicini», so it is not a kinship statement; it is the earliest evidence that the two houses the line would later join were already neighbours.

«Sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino del Defunto» — declaring atto 30, the death of Giuseppe Cossi, aged one, son of Francesco Cossi. THE FOURTH CHILD OF THAT HOUSEHOLD he has declared (1823, 1824, 1825, 1827); the register calls him «vicino» every time and never «parente». NOTE THE AGE: 37 in 1817, 40 in 1825, 46 twice in 1826, 40 here — and the trade slides from massaro di campagna to massaro to colono. Either the clerks guessed or there are two Giuseppe Falco on that street.

«Sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni CINQUANTASEI, di professione POSSIDENTE, domiciliato in strada Camellara, PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA» — atto 54, on the death of Mariantonia Cossi, seven months, daughter of Francesco Cossi and Maria Falco. THE FIFTH CHILD OF THAT HOUSE HE HAS DECLARED, and the FIRST TIME THE REGISTER CALLS HIM PARENTE rather than vicino. The kinship between Maria Falco and this Giuseppe Falco is now stated by the record; the degree is not. Caution: he is 56 and a possidente here, against 40 and a colono eighteen months earlier — either the clerks guessed, or there are two Giuseppe Falco on that street.

Declared by CESARE COSSI, 30, and FRANCESCO COSSI, 34, both of strada Camellara — and Francesco Cossi is very likely the husband of the Maria Falco for whose three dead children Giuseppe Falco had stood in 1823, 1824 and 1825. Aged thirty-two, so born about 1794 — which sits between, and matches neither of, the two Maria Falco baptisms of 1789 and 1790 in this house. Either an age given loosely, or a third daughter of the name.
«Maria Falco figlia delli fu Giuseppe Falco e Rosa Sossi, vedova di Francesco Quotolo» — died at twelve o'clock. No age is given; the 1816–18 form does not ask for one.
the act that names this marriage is her own death act; no children are named

«e Maria Falco» — «delli fu» governs both parents, so she too was dead by February 1818. A FALCO WOMAN MARRIED INTO THE MAJONE. Whether she is the Maria Falco buried on 24 July 1817 — «figlia delli fu Giuseppe Falco e Rosa Sossi, vedova di Francesco Quotolo» — is NOT established. One woman twice widowed would fit the dates; so would two women of the same name. Nothing here decides it.

«e di MARIA FALCO, domiciliata ivi» — A LIVING MARIA FALCO in 1823, and therefore a third woman of the name. She is not the Maria Falco buried on 24 July 1817 (daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Rosa Sossi, widow of Francesco Quotolo), nor the Maria Falco who was already dead in February 1818 as the mother of Angela Majone. Her own parents are not named here. The declarant is GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, who gives himself as a «vicino» and not as kin — so nothing in the act joins her to the line.

«figlia di FRANCESCO COSSI, di professione contadino, e di MARIA FALCO» — and the declarant Giuseppe Falco is «PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA». After five acts calling him only a neighbour, the register states the kinship. This is the evidence the archive's open question on the third Maria Falco was waiting for.

«MARIA FALCO d'anni trentadue, MOGLIE DI ALFONSO DIGLIO … figlia di PASQUALE FALCO … e di CHIARA RIVETTI» — a daughter of the direct line's generation two. Declared by Angelo Sansone, 45, and Tomaso Sposito, 50, both contadini of strada Camellara, each as «vicino», not «parente».

line.name: Matteo Falco
line.note: Named as the father in the baptisms of at least five children at Arienzo between 1767 and 1786, and again in his son Giuseppe's marriage record. He appears as a witness at an Arienzo marriage in 1759, so he was an adult by then. He replaces the Agostino Falcone previously carried at the head of this line. **A third child, found in 1822, names them again — and earliest of all.** On 17 October 1822 **ANGELA FALCO**, fifty-one, widow of Crescenzo Rivetti, died on strada Capodiuomo, «figlia di MATTEO FALCO Defunto, di professione Contadino, e di FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta». Born about 1771. The founding couple is now named from the death acts of THREE separate children — Angela's in 1822, Rosa's in 1830 and Pasquale's in 1834 — and Angela's is the earliest. It also resolves an act found earlier in this research: when her husband Crescenzo Rivetti died in December 1816, **Gioacchino Falco** and **Giuseppe Falco** declared it as «parenti del defunto». They were his wife's brothers — which makes **Gioacchino Falco a strong candidate for a fifth child of Matteo and Francesca**, though no record yet names his parents.

THE ONLY FALCO IN TWENTY ANNUAL REGISTERS DESCRIBED AS A POSSIDENTE, and not on strada Camellara. He carries the founding ancestor's name; nothing yet names his father. UNJOINED to this line.

«è morto nella sua propria casa MATTEO FALCO D'ANNI DUE, nato in Arienzo» — died at ten at night on 24 August 1842, aged two, so born about 1840. HIS NAME IS THE QUESTION. Neapolitan custom named a first son for his father's father, and the name at the head of this line is MATTEO FALCO, who married Francesca Crisci. That is a reason to look for Michele among Matteo's sons. IT IS NOT EVIDENCE. A naming habit is not a record, and this archive does not build a generation out of one.

Named WITHOUT «fu», so alive. A contadino on strada Camellara, the street of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti. NO ACT NAMES HIS PARENTS. He is not placed in the line here, and the archive will not place him until an act does.

name: Pasquale Falco

events.evidence: è morto nella sua propria casa Pasquale Falco, d'anni settantaquattro, marito di Chiara Rivetti, di professione contadino, nato in Arienzo, figlio di Matteo Falco, defunto, e di Francesca Crisci, defunta

On his daughter Anna's death act he is «PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — WITHOUT «fu» or «defunto». So he was alive on 23 August 1820, a contadino, living on strada Camellara, fourteen years before his own death act of 1 October 1834. This is an independent civil sighting of the ancestor between his marriage and his death.

«sono comparsi PASQUALE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque, di professione COLONO, regnicolo, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara, vicino del defunto, e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — atto 8. THE ONLY RECORD IN WHICH PASQUALE FALCO ACTS FOR HIMSELF. Every other sighting has him named by somebody else: on his children's acts, or on his own death act of 1834. Here he walks into the town hall with his brother Giuseppe and reports a neighbour's child dead. He is fifty-five, which against his baptism of 24 October 1767 is one year out — ordinary. And his trade is given as COLONO, a tenant farmer, where his death act of 1834 calls him contadino.

Named without «fu» in his daughter Maria's death act, and still a CONTADINO. The second civil sighting of him alive between his 1780s marriage and his death on 1 October 1834; the first is Anna's act of August 1820.

line.name: Pasquale (Pascuale) Falco
line.note: Baptised in the Collegiate Church of Sant'Andrea at Arienzo on 24 October 1767 — the record names his father Matteo and his mother Francesca Crisci. He married Chiara Rivetti and their children were baptised in the same church from 1789 to 1802. He died at five in the morning on 1 October 1834 at his own house on strada Camellara; the civil act, given by two neighbours, names him husband of Chiara Rivetti and son of the late Matteo Falco and the late Francesca Crisci — confirming the 1767 baptism from an entirely separate record series. It gives his age as 74, which the baptism does not support; stated ages in these registers are approximate. **A daughter found in 1820 adds a third independent sighting.** On 23 August 1820 his daughter **ANNA FALCO**, twenty-five, wife of Arcangelo Crisci, died on strada Camellara, and her act names her «figlia di PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, e di CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — **both parents WITHOUT «fu»**. So Pasquale was alive, a contadino, and on the family's street in August 1820, fourteen years before his own death act; and Chiara, whom no record but her 1843 burial had ever named, was alive beside him. Anna was born about 1795 and had buried a two-day-old son seven months earlier. **And once, in 1824, he speaks for himself.** On 25 March 1824 the register opens: «sono comparsi **PASQUALE FALCO**, di anni **cinquantacinque**, di professione **COLONO**, regnicolo, domiciliato in questo comune, **strada Camellara**, vicino del defunto, e **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — the two brothers together, reporting a neighbour's five-year-old dead. **It is the only record in which Pasquale acts rather than being named**: everywhere else somebody else is speaking of him. It gives his trade as *colono*, a tenant farmer, where his death act ten years later calls him *contadino*; and his age as fifty-five, one year out against the baptism of 1767, which is ordinary in these registers. **HER PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED BY A CIVIL ACT.** She died on 3 September 1843 at eight in the evening, in her own house, aged eighty, a *contadina*: «CHIARA RIVETTI VEDOVA DI PASQUALE FALCO … figlia di NICOLA RIVETTI defunto, di professione CONTADINO, e di ANNA DI RUGGIO defunta». The archive had carried two rival couples for her parents since 2026 — the gentry Don Nicola Rivetti and Donn'Anna Quotolo, and the labouring Nicola Rivetti and Anna di Ruggio — and had said the labouring couple was the better fit without claiming it. The act settles it: her father was a contadino.

civil act 47, foglio 149: «è comparso Vincenzo Falco, di anni ventisette, contadino, strada Camellara… è nato nella sua propria casa, da lui dichiarante e da Andreana Crisci sua moglie legittima, d'anni venti, un maschio… a cui si è dato il nome di Raffaele» — born at three in the afternoon

«è comparso Vincenzo Falco, di anni trentacinque, bracciale… strada Camellara… da Andreana Crisci sua moglie legittima, d'anni venticinque, un maschio… a cui si è dato il nome di Raffaele» — a FIRST child of this name, two years before the Raffaele of 10 May 1818. Ordinarily the first died; which of the two is generation four is now an open question

«Raffaele Falco figlio di Vincenzo Falco, e d'Andreana Crisci» — died at seven in the morning, aged about eighteen months. THIS IS THE BURIAL OF THE FIRST RAFFAELE, born 25 April 1816, and it settles generation four: the Raffaele of 10 May 1818 is the one who lived. Declared by Sabato Vassallo, 26, sportellaro of strada Porta di Sopra, and by GIUSEPPE FALCO, 37, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara, the two of them «PARENTI» — kin.

line.name: Raffaele Falco
line.note: Baptised at Arienzo in 1818 — “ex Vincentio Falco, e Andreana Crisci coniugibus huius Parochiae, cui imposuit nomen Raphael”, with Gelsumina Ruggiero as godmother. His death record of 21 April 1880 names his father as Vincenzo. His wife Angela Rosa Morgillo, daughter of Orazio, died six days before him. His civil birth act — Arienzo, act 47 of 10 May 1818 — has him born at three in the afternoon in his father's own house on strada Camellara, and gives both parents' ages: Vincenzo twenty-seven, Andreana Crisci twenty. It is the first record to date her at all, putting her birth about 1798 and her marriage, in December 1814, at about sixteen. **The complication is now closed.** Vincenzo and Andreana had named an earlier son Raffaele on 25 April 1816, and for a time this archive could not say which of the two was generation four — the generation was carried as *disputed*. The 1817 death register settles it: on **28 October 1817** the first Raffaele was buried, «figlio di Vincenzo Falco, e d'Andreana Crisci», aged about eighteen months. The child of 10 May 1818 is the one who lived. The burial was declared by **Giuseppe Falco, 37, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara**, called a «parente» of the family — a documented son of Matteo, and so Vincenzo's uncle. One warning survives: the two birth acts give irreconcilable ages for the father, Vincenzo thirty-five in 1816 and twenty-seven in 1818.

line.name: Raffaele Falco
line.note: A farmer of Arienzo. His last recorded child, Gerardo, was born in 1913 not at Arienzo but at Arpaia, over the provincial border — the first sign of the move north.

events.evidence: daughter of Matteo Falco and Francesca Crisci — a sister of Pasquale, and therefore of the direct line
ex Mattheo Falco, et Francisca Crisci ... quae nominata est Rosa
Rosa Falco, d'anni quarantadue, moglie di Carlantonio Morgillo, nata in Arienzo, contadina, figlia di Matteo Falco, defunto, e di Francesca Crisci, defunta — matches the Rosa baptised 5 Jan 1786

«Rosaria Falco figlia di Giuseppe Falco, e Gelsomina Vigliotta» — died at twenty-three hours THE SAME DAY as her brother Domenico, eleven hours after him. No birth act has been found for her: she is not in the Arienzo birth registers of 1816, 1817 or 1818, so she was born earlier. Declared by a neighbour of strada Sossi and Francesco Martone, 47, cantiniere, of strada Camellara.

line.name: Vincenzo Falco
line.note: His civil marriage act — Arienzo, act 26 of 15 December 1814 — records him as aged 21, a contadino, and “figlio maggiore di Pasquale Falco”: eldest son, and his father named without “fu”, so Pasquale was still living. His wife Andreana is “figlia di Arcangelo”. The parish record of the same marriage names his mother Chiara Rivetti and Andreana's mother Ruggiero. His death record of 15 May 1875 names Pasquale a third time. The civil death registers place his household on strada Camellara at Arienzo, the same street as his father’s, and name him with his wife Andreana Crisci. He called a son Pasquale after his father twice: the first died aged three on 22 February 1833, while the grandfather still lived; the second was born about a fortnight after the grandfather’s death and lived ten days, dying on Christmas Day 1834.

«Angela, seu Lella Majone, figlia delli fu Nicola Majone, e Maria Falco, moglie di Giuseppe Sossi» — died at nineteen hours. «seu» = «or», the register giving both the formal name and the one she was called by.

«e di MARIA ROSA MAURO, domiciliata ivi»

events.place: Arienzo, strada Trave, later strada Cappuccini
events.evidence: JOINED. The 1816 register (atto 23) buries GAETANA LAUDATO, 78, «vedova di SIMONE MORGILLO», of strada Trave, and the declarants are ANGELO MORGILLO, 58, of that street and Giuseppe Morgillo, «figlio della defunta». Angelo at 58 in 1816 is exactly the ANGELO MORGILLO, 70, COLONO of strada Cappuccini who declares in 1828 and heads the Monticello de' Cappuccini household. So this man and the head of that house are the same, and his parents are SIMONE MORGILLO and GAETANA LAUDATO (b. c. 1738).

«ANGELO MORGILLO, di anni SETTANTA, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in strada Cappuccini» — declaring atto 56. Born about 1758. A SECOND Angelo Morgillo, distinct from the Angelo, 58, of strada Nuova di San Gaetano buried in October 1826; the distinction resolves the age conflict raised by Saveria Morgillo's act of 1827, whose father he is very likely to be.

His parents, from the 1816 register: SIMONE MORGILLO and GAETANA LAUDATO, who died on 9 March 1816 aged seventy-eight, «vedova di Simone Morgillo», of strada Trave. Angelo declared it himself, aged fifty-eight — which is exactly seventy in 1828.

events.place: Arienzo, strada Nuova di San Gaetano
events.evidence: «figlia di BIAGIO MORGILLO, di professione contadino, e di VINCENZA VECE» — atto 11. He is the Biagio Morgillo, 30, who declared his own father Angelo Morgillo's death in October 1826 as «figlio del defunto».

named as the husband on his wife's death act of 1830. His age will not settle: three sightings inside twenty months give thirty (Feb 1816), thirty-six (Oct 1816) and thirty-three (Sept 1817) — «Carlantonio Morgillo, di anni trentatre, bracciale, strada Maddalena». Birth therefore somewhere in 1780×1786; this archive formerly printed «about 1784» from the 1817 act alone, which overstated it. Constant across all three: bracciale, and the household on strada Maddalena in 1817, thirteen years before Rosa died on strada Camellara.

«Carlantonio Morgillo, di anni trentatre, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Maddalena» — declaring the death of GIUDITTA MORGILLO as «vicino, parente», with Matteo Migliore of San Felice. A FOURTH sighting, and it tightens the age: thirty-three in September 1817 and thirty-three again in August 1818, against thirty in February 1816 and thirty-six in October 1816. The two later readings agree on a birth about 1784–85. AND A LEAD: Giuditta is daughter of the LATE Carlantonio Morgillo and Manilia Rivetti, and this Carlantonio declares her death as kin. He is very plausibly her brother, which would give this man's own parents. The act says «parente» without saying how, so it is not asserted.

«Carlantonio Morgillo, di anni trentacinque, contadino» — a FIFTH sighting. Thirty-three in August 1818 and thirty-five fourteen months later: fast by a year, but the run 33 (Sept 1817), 33 (Aug 1818), 35 (Oct 1819) is broadly consistent and keeps the birth around 1784-85. The outliers remain the two 1816 readings, thirty and thirty-six.

«figlia delli fu Carlantonio Morgillo» — dead by August 1818. A SECOND Carlantonio Morgillo, and the discovery matters: the Carlantonio Morgillo who married Rosa Falco was alive in 1830, and declares this very act aged thirty-three. Two men of the name, one generation apart.

«GENNARO MORGILLO, vedovo di Felicia Sompone, nato in Arienzo, di anni cinquantatré, di professione COLONO, domiciliato STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di ANGELO MORGILLO defunto, di professione COLONO» — born about 1790. A THIRD SON of the colono Angelo, and the one who left the hill: he lived on strada Camellara, the Falco street. HIS DEATH WAS DECLARED BY GIUSEPPE FALCO, colono of the same street. It is the closest the record comes to the Falco-Morgillo marriage that was still thirty years away.
«Giuditta Morgillo figlia delli fu Carlantonio Morgillo, e Manilia Rivetti, vedova di Giuseppe Gimbardo» — died at sixteen hours
«figlio di Giuseppe Morgillo» — no «fu», so alive in July 1818
named as his wife — another Morgillo–Rivetti marriage

34 in 1828, contadino. Husband of Maria Majone; their eight-year-old Raffaele died in May (atto 14). He declares his brother's child's death as «zio della defunta» (atto 56), which makes him and Vincenzo brothers.

«e di Orazio Morgillo, di anni ventisei, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Travo» — born about 1792. A LEAD, NOT A LINK: generation four's wife, Angela Rosa Morgillo, is recorded as a daughter of an ORAZIO Morgillo and was born 24 February 1818 — when a man of this age would have been twenty-six. But she was born at SAN FELICE, not Arienzo, and Orazio is not rare enough to assume. This is the first Orazio Morgillo this archive has met in any record.
«Pasquale Morgillo figlio di Giuseppe Morgillo, e Gelsomina Rivetti» — died at ten in the morning; no age given

«e di Giovanna Perrotta» — named as living, no age given

Defunta» — atto 20. Eighty-eight, so born about 1736. «Giuseppe Quotolo, di anni sessantacinque, di professione massaro di campagna, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Maddalena» — declaring Maria Falco's death as a parente, with Aniello Diglio, 45, contadino. «Pietro Quotolo, di anni trenta, di professione massaro di campagna, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Maddalena». Born about 1787.

«marito di Giustina Morgillo»

He is recorded as a household of one because a priest has no wife; «father» is only the schema's word for a head.

«e Gelsomina Rivetti» — a THIRD Morgillo–Rivetti marriage: the two families the Falco married also married each other
«e Manilia Rivetti» — «delli fu» governs both. A fourth Morgillo–Rivetti marriage in these registers.
«e Michedalena Rivetti» — the scribe breaks the name across a line as «e Miche-/dalena», a Campanian blend of Michela and Maddalena. A Rivetti woman married into the di Guida.

«figlia di NICOLA RIVETTI defunto, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato ivi» — from his daughter Chiara's civil death act of 3 September 1843, read at full resolution. THE TRADE IS THE POINT: he is a contadino, not a Don. That rules out the gentry couple, Don Nicola Rivetti and Donn'Anna Quotolo, which this archive had carried as the rival candidate since 2026.

«figlio di NICOLA RIVETTI Defunto, di professione Contadino» — a CONTADINO Nicola Rivetti, dead by September 1821. THE BEST CANDIDATE YET FOR CHIARA RIVETTI'S FATHER: Chiara, who married Pasquale Falco, is «filia quondam NICOLAI et ANNA» in her 1843 Latin burial entry and was born about 1763; this Nicola's son Carmine was born about 1768. Same forename, same generation, and the same station — Chiara married a contadino.
«marito di ANGELA ESPOSITELLA» — brother of Crescenzo Rivetti, who married Angela Falco

«è morto nella sua propria casa PAOLO RIVETTI, di anni cinquanta, marito di ANGELA ESPOSITELLA, nato in Arienzo, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Fontana, figlio di PASQUALE RIVETTI Defunto, di professione contadino, e di GIOVANNA PERROTTA, domiciliata ivi» — the same couple named as CRESCENZO RIVETTI's parents in the act of 1 December 1816. So Paolo is Crescenzo's BROTHER, and therefore Angela Falco's brother-in-law. Born about 1773. Declared by GIOVANNI RIVETTI, 23, POSSIDENTE of strada Capodiuomo, as «NIPOTE» — nephew — which ties the propertied Rivetti of that street to this family.
«figlio del fu Pasquale Rivetti» — dead by December 1816

name: Suor Maria Maddalena Rivetti
household: Don Giuseppe Rivetti (the elder) & Giovanna Bega

events.evidence: «Suor Maria Maddalena Rivetti figlia delli fu Don Giuseppe Rivetti, e Giovanna Bega» — a nun, died at twenty-two hours. The third and clearest sign of a Rivetti house of standing at Arienzo, beside Donna Francesca Rivetti of 1816, the apothecary Don Giovanbattista, and the priest Don Giuseppe.

Seventy-six, «DI PROFESSIONE ARCIPRETE» — the archpriest of Arienzo, born about 1766. This archive has been reading Latin parish burial entries from Arienzo for months; the man who presided over the parish through most of that period now has a name, an age and a family. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH is that he wrote any particular entry: an archpriest presides, curates write. Chiara Rivetti's 1843 burial entry was made after his death.

A POSSIDENTE, dead before 1840. Named in two death acts a generation apart, with the same rank and trade both times: as father of MARIA GIUSEPPA SCARPATI (Morti 1840 atto 28) and as father of DON ANGELO SCARPATI, ARCIPRETE OF ARIENZO (Morti 1842 atto 15).

Seventy-two, «DI PROFESSIONE SORORA DEL CONSERVATORIO», died «NEL CONSERVATORIO DI SAN FILIPPO [NERI]» — a SECOND religious house in Arienzo, distinct from the Ave Gratia Plena where every other institutional death in these registers happens. Atto 46 of the same volume names a STRADA SAN FILIPPO NERI, which corroborates the dedication from the other direction. Born about 1768.
«moglie di Giuseppe Sossi» — alive in February 1818, no age given
«e Rosa Sossi» — «delli fu» governs both parents, so she too was dead by July 1817. The Sossi are one of the largest families in the 1817 register.
